def: A short document, signed by both sides before the evaluation is run, that fixes the decision, the gold set, the metrics, the pass rule and the run procedure.
A collection of real inputs from the customer's own work, each paired with the correct output as decided by people the customer trusts.
A range that, if the measurement were repeated on fresh random cases many times, would contain the true value about 95% of the time.
Written instructions, with examples, for who labels a gold set, whether labellers work independently and how disagreements are settled.
A kind of mistake that must stay below a hard limit whatever the average accuracy, because a single one is a serious incident.
The average cost of a system's errors per item handled, found by weighting each error type by what it costs the customer.
The claim that a new system is no worse than the current one by more than an agreed margin, which needs less evidence than proving it better.
